text: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand the nature of your discomfort and fertility challenges, have you experienced any pain during urination or noticed any unusual discharge from your vagina?

speaker: Patient
text: 30-year-old female. The patient and her husband have been trying to conceive for 15 months without success. They are sexually active at least twice a week. The husband occasionally has difficulties maintaining an erection. The patient reports discomfort and pelvic floor muscle tension during attempted vaginal penetration. Diagnosed with body dysmorphic disorder three years ago. No family history of serious illness. She is a non-smoker and does not drink alcohol. No medications.

speaker: Doctor

That pelvic floor tension during penetration is significant; is this pain localized to the vaginal opening or deeper inside, and does it prevent you from completing sexual intercourse entirely? Additionally, have you experienced any episodes of fever, foul-smelling discharge, or abnormal bleeding?

text: All other systems reviewed are within normal limits. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Multiple sclerosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is an unusual suggestion from your previous doctor; Multiple Sclerosis does not present with difficulty conceiving or pain specifically during vaginal penetration. Based on your description of pelvic floor muscle tension preventing penetration and your history of trying to conceive, are you willing to try topical estrogen or physical therapy for possible Vulvodynia or Vaginismus? Please let me know if you have any specific fears about these treatments, and confirm if you have had any prior pelvic surgeries.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Vulvodynia / Vaginismus (likely secondary to body dysmorphic disorder or chronic pelvic pain syndrome).
